Hi Sam — attaching the requested artifacts to this thread and placing the originals in the shared Clearline Drive folder: https://drive.redwoodinc.com/shared/clearline/sig-artifacts

Attachments (stubs):
- hsm-attestation-20260614.pdf (HSM vendor attestation; includes FIPS 140-2 level information and HSM model family)
- kms-rotation-log-2026Q1.csv (rotation events, timestamps, key alias, redacted key ID column)
- network-encryption-diagram.png (high-level schema: customer tenant boundaries, envelope encryption flow)
- redwood-sig-checklist.xlsx (matrix mapping artifacts to SIG/CAIQ questions)

Summary of key points:
- Keys are stored in hardware-backed HSMs (CloudHSM-v2 cluster). Master KEKs are wrapped by HSM and never exported in plaintext.
- Envelope encryption: data encryption keys (DEKs) generated per-tenant, wrapped with KEK; KEKs are rotated on a 12-month cadence unless customer requests more frequent rotation. Ephemeral session keys rotate per-issue or per-batch as configured.
- Rotation logs include UTC timestamps and operator/service IDs; we have redacted direct key material from the export.
- Backup/escrow: we maintain sealed backups for KEKs encrypted with customer-specific wrapping; emergency rotation procedure is documented in the runbook referenced in the checklist.
- TLS: endpoints enforce TLS1.2+ with a preferred cipher suite list (TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384). Inter-service traffic uses mTLS with mutual cert rotation.

Notes about the logs: to protect secrets, the export contains key aliases and rotation event metadata only (no raw key material). If Clearline needs additional fields (e.g., exact operator user IDs or expanded audit traces) we'll need a signed data-access attestation and timeboxed access window.

If this packaging looks good I'll move the Drive folder to the external-sharing ACL and send a presigned link. Let me know if you prefer SFTP instead.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
